title: Word Search II
prompt:
Given an `m x n` board of letters and a list of `words`, return all words that can be formed by a path of horizontally/vertically adjacent cells (no cell reused within a word).

**Example**: board `[["o","a","a","n"],["e","t","a","e"],["i","h","k","r"],["i","f","l","v"]]`, words `["oath","pea","eat","rain"]` → `["oath","eat"]`.

Searching each word separately is too slow. Load all words into a trie and DFS the board once, walking the trie in lockstep.

tests.note: would need to reuse a cell

hints: Insert every word into a trie; store the full word at its end node.
DFS from each cell, descending both the board and the trie by the current letter. If the trie node has no matching child, prune immediately.
When a node holds a word, add it and clear it (to avoid duplicates). Mark cells visited with a sentinel and restore on backtrack.

solution.explanation: The trie collapses the whole word list into one shared prefix tree, so a single board DFS finds all words simultaneously and prunes the moment the current path isn't a prefix of any word — far better than O(words × board-DFS). Sinking visited cells to `#` enforces no-reuse within a path.
